properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 29 at 10:22PM MDT until July 29 at 10:30PM MDT by NWS Grand Junction CO
properties.description:
The Flood Advisory will expire at 1030 PM MDT this evening for a
portion of west central Colorado, including the following areas,
Delta, Mesa and Montrose.

Excess runoff from heavy rain has ended over the warned area. If
flooding has been observed...Please report it to your local law
enforcement agency. Arroyo and small stream flooding is no longer
expected to pose a threat. Please continue to heed remaining road
closures.
properties.areaDesc: Delta, CO; Mesa, CO; Montrose, CO

properties.headline: Flood Advisory issued July 29 at 10:03PM MDT until July 30 at 1:00AM MDT by NWS Denver CO
properties.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is expected.

* WHERE...Southeastern Lincoln County in east central Colorado...

* WHEN...Until 100 AM MDT.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding in low-lying and poor drainage areas.
Rises in small streams and normally dry creeks.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...

- At 1003 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated heavy rain due to
thunderstorms. Minor flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly in the advisory area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain have
fallen.

- Additional rainfall amounts of 0.5 to 1 inch are expected over
the area. This additional rain will result in minor flooding.

- Some locations that will experience flooding include...
Wild Horse Point.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 9:00PM MDT until July 30 at 12:00AM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Crowley County in southeastern Colorado...
Northwestern Otero County in southeastern Colorado...
Northeastern Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until midnight MDT.

* At 900 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2 inches of rain
have fallen. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Rocky Ford, Fowler, Ordway, Swink, Manzanola, Olney Springs, Sugar
City and Crowley.
properties.areaDesc: Crowley, CO; Otero, CO; Pueblo, CO

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 8:10PM MDT until July 29 at 11:15PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
The Willow Burn Scar in...
Central Lake County in central Colorado...

* Until 1115 PM MDT.

* At 810 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms produced heavy
rain over the Willow Burn Scar. Up to 0.5 inches of rain have
fallen. Flooding impacts will continue, but no additional rainfall
is expected. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly. Excessive rainfall over the burn scar will result in
debris flow moving through the Rock Creek, WIllow Creek, Rock Creek
Trail and near the Leadville National Fish Hatchery. The debris
flow can consist of rock, mud, vegetation and other loose
materials.

HAZARD...Life threatening flash flooding. Thunderstorms producing
flash flooding in and around the Willow Burn Scar.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Life threatening flash flooding of areas in and around the
Willow Burn Scar.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Turquoise Lake.

properties.headline: Flash Flood Warning issued July 29 at 8:03PM MDT until July 29 at 11:00PM MDT by NWS Pueblo CO
properties.description:
FFWPUB

The National Weather Service in Pueblo has issued a

* Flash Flood Warning for...
Northeastern Huerfano County in southeastern Colorado...
Northwestern Las Animas County in southeastern Colorado...
Southeastern Pueblo County in southeastern Colorado...

* Until 1100 PM MDT.

* At 803 PM MDT, Doppler radar indicated thunderstorms producing
heavy rain across the warned area. Between 1 and 2.5 inches of rain
have fallen. The expected rainfall rate is 1 to 2 inches in 1 hour.
Additional rainfall amounts of 1 to 2 inches are possible in the
warned area. Flash flooding is ongoing or expected to begin
shortly.

HAZARD...Flash flooding caused by thunderstorms.

SOURCE...Radar indicated.

IMPACT...Flash flooding of small creeks and streams, urban areas,
highways, streets and underpasses as well as other poor
drainage and low-lying areas.

* Some locations that will experience flash flooding include...
Mainly rural areas of Northeastern Huerfano, Northwestern Las
Animas and Southeastern Pueblo Counties.
